selected_mathematical_checks: The initial flag has a=1/D and b=D^(n-1)V, so b/a=D^n V is an integer. The displayed matrix has determinant -1 and sends the vertices of the second axis simplex, after translation by b e_n, to exactly the second cell. This pays integral unimodularity for every real cut t without denominator loss.

Strict block envelope inequalities allow contractions sigma_j>1/2 with capacities still above A_j. The smallest local intercept is at least min(a,eta b)/2, leaving room below the I136 /100 entrance for the asserted /400 threshold. Selected supports lie in fixed compact interiors of the original P; rounding translations costs O(1) exponents and is absorbed for all sufficiently large k.

For finite selected supports, phi=max(ell_1,ell_2) and the stated torus scaling, column multiplier and block-row multiplier give exactly z^(phi(u)-ell_j(u)). Exponents vanish on the assigned block and are positive on the other. The square minor tends to a block diagonal matrix with nonzero determinant. This establishes simultaneous rank, rather than inferring it from separate block ranks.

For rational closure enlarge the cut interval to [eta/2,1-eta/2]. Its minimum intercept is at least half the previous one; contractions can be chosen sufficiently close to one so the /400 entrance remains below local /100. Countably many rational weights/cuts and finitely many partitions at fixed r give a common very-general locus before real limits. Boundary nefness does not assert jet separation exactly at the volume boundary.

For the 2:1 family in dimension three, the block costs are exactly 8V/9 and V/9, and the maximum weight tends to zero with N. Thus A139 reaches all sufficiently large N, without divisibility, and includes the prior .99 example. The earlier method obstructions are not contradicted.

In the singleton slender cell, restriction to a one-dimensional subtorus gives exponent span at most kc+O(1); ordinary order floor(kw) jets require at least floor(kw)+1 independent one-dimensional jets. Exact capacity c=w^n/a^(n-1)<w for w<a makes this impossible. Torus translations and integral unimodular changes retain the tested width obstruction. It is not an obstruction to all shapes.

Normal-cone deformation uses algebraic arcs after an etale base change, with distinct central bubble points away from the attaching hyperplanes. Section blowups are in the smooth locus over the base, so the family stays flat and projective. The total pullback of each bubble divisor restricts to the exceptional divisor on the main component and to -H on its bubble; the section exceptional divisors do not meet the main component. Hence the stated divisor restrictions are exactly the prescribed nef classes.

Adding rational epsilon times a relatively ample divisor makes each central component restriction ample, hence the central-fibre restriction ample. Openness and a countable choice of epsilon give nefness on a generic or suitable ordinary complex noncentral fibre. The relative Hilbert-scheme argument then supplies a very-general tuple on the original X. Real coefficients are approximated from below so starting nef classes remain nef.

The mth-power morphism has m^n distinct unramified preimages of a torus point over C. The pullback of hyperplanes through the point generates its reduced fibre ideal twisted by mH, giving mH-sum F globally generated on the blowup. This independently supplies exact branch sizes m^n.

Finite refinement multiplies weights and preserves the sum of nth powers. For N divisible by eight, 9N/8 equal roots with N retained and N/8 split eightfold produce exactly N large and N small leaves. For odd N, 2/(3N) is not a reciprocal integer; fixed positive target coordinates cannot be limits of other reciprocal integers, which are locally finite there. Downward domination at full volume forces equality. This excludes the equal-root/equal-branch method, not unequal bubble inputs or combinations with A139.
